Ramaphosa vs Magashule... Extra time

By: Sophia Phirippides | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The ANC is going into extra time in the contest between President Cyril Ramaphosa and Secretary General Ace Magashule. Both have ordered the suspension of the other, a tight match is poised at 1-1.

Unique Selling Point:
Ace has set out his game plan with his affidavit lodged at the Gauteng High Court. He is appealing his suspension, citing rule 25.70 of the ANC Constitution, which incorporates the step-aside rule, arguing that it was not implemented in accordance with ANC resolutions - and restates that constitutionally he should be regarded as innocent until proven guilty. Could this prove to be a massive own goal scored by the ANC?

Even though he was ordered to stay silent, on 17th May after Former President Zuma’s appearance at the Pietermaritzburg High Court, Magashule went on the attack again - appealing to members (fans) to come en-masse, show their support, on May 26th. Covid-19 restrictions allowing, that day could show if Magashule has actually got the grassroots support, he claims to have, to back up the pressure he is putting on Ramaphosa’s leadership.

On the other side, there is pressure on the ANC to show Magashule the red card. After all, he has refused to step aside and to apologise for trying to suspend President Ramaphosa.

Summary:
What next? Magashule insists that there are processes that haven't been followed and that according to the NEC's resolutions he has not been treated fairly. He is going to appeal. His heart, his mind, his soul belongs to the ANC and according to him, nothing will make him leave his beloved party. He openly accused the Ramaphosa team of buying conference votes at Nasrec for Ramaphosa’s election as leader. Magashule says that there are more dominant factions in the ANC who are getting their way. He sees himself as a victim and as a target of those factions who are out to get Ramaphosa a second term.

In all this subterfuge and confusion does Ace have a point? What can he do next? Are his governing days over, or can he win through in extra-time? To what lengths will he go and what can he actually do, politically and legally?
Outside of the ANC arena, with regards to his court case on the Free State Asbestos charges, Magashule firmly states that he is innocent and has done nothing wrong, that he can't wait for his court case where there will be surprise witnesses.


Story Treatment

We will tell the story using soccer metaphors, interspersing football terms in the narrative:
Goals, own goals, penalties, throw ins, tactics, extra time, injury time, halftime, fulltime whistle, red card, sent off, yellow card, fans, support of the, great save, tackle, foul etc, etc
This is also a reference to how Magashule got the name ‘Ace’ – from his nickname in his old soccer playing days/

An idea for on-camera links is to have the presenter speak into a mic, pitch-side and in the stands sitting like a soccer commentator. We need to find a football field for this where we can also shoot atmospheric shots of the football pitch and goal nets.


Further information:
This is a pivotal moment for the ANC, as President Ramaphosa stands victorious against his arch rival and detractor Magashule, as the ANC stand behind their leader in a show of resolution against corruption and wrong doing. But what skeletons lie in the Ramaphosa cupboard that can come back to haunt him?

As the the ANC is now, who has won and who has lost - have there even been winners and losers or is it a case of gains and losses? The main gain if one looks at it that way is a relook at the existence of the ANC, the raison d'etre versus the power politics and the factionalism. Perhaps we have Ace Magashule to thank for this moment of possible clarity and a new, a real, New Dawn that could emerge from this.

On face value Ramaphosa has doggedly pursued reform of law enforcement agencies like the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA), SA Revenue Service (SARS) and Asset Forfeiture Unit (AFU), to finally drive out corruption, and his competition.

However, in Ramaphosa’s three years plus at the ANC’s helm, the “radical economic transformation” faction have thrived and exploited his weaknesses. These include his wealth and links to big capital, and the dirt within his cleanup faction.

Over the last 27 years we have heard many allegations of corruption within the government all involving multimillion rand deals that go astray. But when we look back, how many of the people who have been implicated have paid the price or been held accountable when facing the law? They can be counted on one hand. The very essence of the corruption and collusion to ensure that those implicated remained untouched, went as far as manipulation of prosecuting authorities.

Recently though there does appear to have been some headway under continued pressure on accused party members - to comply with ANC rules for the sake of solidarity in the movement – for instance, the high profile step aside by Provincial Deputy Chairperson of the ANC in KZN, Mike Mabuyakhulu,.

Carl Niehaus [ Confirmed ]

Political analyst
Swana states that this could be a time of reckoning for the ANC, going back to what Mbekhi said concerning the raison d’etre of the ANC – he suggests the three day retreat that has been suggested is an opportunity for the ANC to look inwardly to politically and morally reformulate the ANC’s core purpose and root out the indemic and systemic corruption – or it might just be used as a platform to cement the divided factions.

Susan Booysen [ confirmed ]
Political analyst

Lawson Naidoo [ confirmed ]
Legal analyst
or
Benedict Phiri
Legal analyst
Will breakdown the veracity of Magashule’s Affidafit and court application for his appeal – some legal analysts believe he has strong grounds for appeal and that the ANC may have blundered.
The ANC are not willing to speak on camera at present but have put out a media response (which we have) that they will oppose Magashule’s application

Press Release:


The Big Match - Team Ramaphosa versus Team Magashule in the Battle for the ANC. Suspended Secretary General Ace Magashule has refused to step aside and to apologise for trying to suspend President Ramaphosa. Will the ANC show him the red card?


Script:


VO: The game is on, two teams are playing for the highest stakes, Team Ramaphosa vs Team Magashule. The prize - control of the ANC.

Link: After months of dithering, the ANC finally moved on its Secretary General Ace Magashule and suspended him. He quickly levelled the score and suspended the president of the party Cyril Ramaphosa, not only that, he's challenging the entire process in court. Could this prove to be a massive own goal by the ANC?

VO: How do the two players’ infringements match up?//
President Cyril Ramaphosa, attempted suspension by Secretary General Ace Magashule for not satisfying the Integrity Commission’s questions on the funds raised for the CR17 election Campaign.

INFRINGEMENTS
NAME: Cyril Ramaphosa
POSITION: President
SUSPENSION: Overruled
ALLEGATIONS: CR17 Funding
Secretary General ACE Magashule: Suspended by the ANC for not stepping aside whilst facing criminal charges, including alleged corruption, fraud and racketeering related to a R250 million rand asbestos audit in the Free State.

INFRINGEMENTS
NAME: “Ace” Magashule
POSITION: Secretary General
SUSPENSION: Enforced
CHARGES: Corruption, fraud and racketeering
BAIL: R200 000
Carl Niehaus: Our National Constitution is very clear. Every citizen is deemed innocent until proven guilty by a court of law

VO: ANC stalwart Carl Niehaus is spokesperson for the Umkhonto We Sizwe Military Veterans Association which is standing behind team Magashule.

Carl: There is legal advice that had been given to the National Executive of the African National Congress, some of that advice came from Dr. Mathews Phosa, who said “the manner in which you are implementing the so called stepping-aside resolution is unconstitutional.”

VO: In an urgent application to the Gauteng High Court, Ace Magashule detailed his objections to his suspension citing unfair implementation of the step aside rule. The ANC has opposed his application in an affidavit by Deputy Secretary General Jessie Duarte, countering that Magashule's challenge is "absurd" and "incoherent" and goes against the party's resolutions.

Carl Niehaus: We believe that in terms of the ANC’s own constitution, that the National Executive of the ANC does not have the powers to amend resolutions of its highest decision making body which are conferences.

VO: Ironically, the step aside resolution in clause 25.70 of the ANC's constitution, formulated to uphold the integrity of people in positions of power, has deepened the divides.
But there may be some merit to the Magashule argument, according to Independent Political Analyst Sandile Swana.

Sandile Swana: Basically, what that rule says, if you are charged by the NPA, criminally charged, then you must step aside, you must be suspended.
Bongani Bingwa: Ace Magashule says he has the right to be presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.
Sandile Swana: Actually the principles of a fair trial are in the ANC Constitution. This an organisation of people who were arrested without trial, detention without trial, so their constitution is very detailed about due process, so that is why many said that this so-called rule 25.70 will never fly, because already it goes against the principles that they wanted.

VO: A major contention in Magashule's affidavit is that the NEC narrowed the scope of the 2017 conference resolution to members charged, rather than merely implicated in criminal acts, targeting Magashule for one.
But the ANC is making a political choice on how to implement the rule as part of a process that goes beyond just Magashule according to Legal Analyst Lawson Naidoo.

Lawson Naidoo: The question that arises, if he does believe that it's unconstitutional, why has he left it until now to challenge that rule when it was adopted such a long time ago, and that will speak to the issue of urgency,. And the court may well say, this is a self created urgency and dismiss his application on the basis of urgency.

VO: Magashule's argument goes further, in that his application appealing the suspension was dismissed by the NEC.

Carl Niehaus: The consequences for him, if that process unfolds in the way it has unfolded for President Zuma is a destruction of his political career, and then at the end, a judge comes and say, No, you're not guilty, as happened with Bongani Bongo.

Lawson Naidoo: The very nature of this stepaside resolution and process is designed as a precautionary measure and in any event, the principle of innocence until proven guilty, is a matter that pertains in criminal litigation, not in civil litigation, which this constitutes. So Mr. Magashule will surely be guaranteed the right to a fair trial. The only thing that the ANC needs to establish here is that he has been charged, therefore the step-aside rule kicks in.

VO: Magashule has been a top scorer in the ANC, rising to the "all powerful position" of Secretary General, and determined to retain that power to the bitter end, he is challenging Ramaphosa head on.

Sandile Swana: So Ace says, I suspended Cyril, because I was satisfied that he has done wrong. That is what he says in his court papers. He must be satisfied as the Secretary General.

Carl: That situation where there are bank accounts of the CR 17 campaign, that are closed, does not become a critical issue for the majority of the National Executive Committee of the ANC to address and that indicates to us there is not even handedness, certain people are being targeted.

Link: Cyril Ramaphosa - enormous wealth, links to big capital. That's his weakness, his detractors say. Ah, but not so fast. The vocal champions of the so called radical economic transformation faction are themselves often accused of corruption. So who has broken the offside rule?

Carl Niehaus: If there are allegations of stealing, let action be taken, but don't equate radical economic transformation with stealing. Radical economic transformation is the official economic policy programme of the ANC.
Bongani Bingwa: But many of its champions within the ANC are the same people who are accused of enabling state capture, for example, to thrive for so long.
Carl Niehaus: Why are those people being accused? Because there’s selective targeting of them, while others who are not promoting radical economic transformation are left off the hook.

VO: President Ramaphosa has been pursuing reform in state law enforcement agencies, empowering them to tackle corruption. Magashule contends that the main goal is to root him out and clear the way for a Ramaphosa triumph in the 2022 ANC elections.

POINT 30 IN MAGASHULE’S AFFIDAVIT
Sandile Swana: But a lot of the success that has been achieved in Cyril getting the majority has been by recruiting the very members of Ace's faction. They know that all the benefits are now with Cyril.

VO: The RET faction is characterised by former President Jacob Zuma. At the resumption of his trial on corruption charges related to the Arms Deal, his disciples within the ANC, including Magashule, made a show of force,( … sound ups on Ace.. Ace chant…) and the fans rallied behind them. (crowd shots etc..
Vox: I support the SG because he’s our general secretary elected in the conference until we are told that he is guilty by doing 1-2-3,then we will decide otherwise then.
VO: The Zuma trial is proving to be a convenient platform for the RET faction to galvanise their supporters. Political analyst, Professor Susan Booysen, maintains that radical economic transformation in their hands lacks credibility.

Susan Booysen: I've just seen too many years where they have been doing virtually nothing.
Bongani Bingwa: The RET faction says it's not for lack of trying. Zuma tried his best, he tried infrastructure development, he tried free education. All of those now are being rolled back.
Susan Booysen: I believe certainly infrastructure development were, had as much attention in Mbeki's days as well. It was not a zuma invention. It was a grand exit point of Zuma to bring in, fee free education at a time and in a way when he needed, really needed something to build his legacy

Link: Ace Magashule's suspension was the yellow card, but he's carried on the attack. It's the ultimate game of brinkmanship. So will he be shown the red card?

Sandile Swana: Politically it's tricky, because you must look at the tactics of Cyril Ramaphosa, because he's the one who fired Malema, so he is unlikely to repeat that mistake.So I think that they will want to cut the wings of Ace and make him a very tame entity inside the ANC.

Carl: The Secretary General will not be out of the game. This is not a football game. This is a liberation movement with a membership, and ultimately, it is not some referee with a set of cards in his upper pocket who will determine the future, but the members of the African National Congress.

Bongani Bingwa:. If it were to go Ace Magashule's way, that would be a headache for the party.
Lawson Naidoo: It would set a precedent, then the ANC would be effectively back to square one in how they're going to deal with corrupt elements within their membership.

Battle for the ANC Roundup
Susan Booysen: All indications are that the Magashule team hasn't got what it takes to clinch those goals. I think Ramaphosa's people believe they're lining up because they've had territorial advantage for much of the game. And it is really not a pretty sight to see these two [unclear] teams play,and there is going to be a winner at this stage. It looks like the Ramaphosa people.

Carl: There is legal advice that had been given to the National Executive of the African National Congress, some of that advice came from Dr. Mathews Phosa, who said “the manner in which you are implementing the so called stepping-aside resolution is unconstitutional.” VO: In an urgent application to the Gauteng High Court, Ace Magashule detailed his objections to his suspension citing unfair implementation of the step aside rule. The ANC has opposed his application in an affidavit by Deputy Secretary General Jessie Duarte, countering that Magashule's challenge is "absurd" and "incoherent" and goes against the party's resolutions. Carl Niehaus: We believe that in terms of the ANC’s own constitution, that the National Executive of the ANC does not have the powers to amend resolutions of its highest decision making body which are conferences. VO: Ironically, the step aside resolution in clause 25.70 of the ANC's constitution, formulated to uphold the integrity of people in positions of power, has deepened the divides. But there may be some merit to the Magashule argument, according to Independent Political Analyst Sandile Swana. Sandile Swana: Basically, what that rule says, if you are charged by the NPA, criminally charged, then you must step aside, you must be suspended. Bongani Bingwa: Ace Magashule says he has the right to be presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law. Sandile Swana: Actually the principles of a fair trial are in the ANC Constitution. This an organisation of people who were arrested without trial, detention without trial, so their constitution is very detailed about due process, so that is why many said that this so-called rule 25.70 will never fly, because already it goes against the principles that they wanted. VO: A major contention in Magashule's affidavit is that the NEC narrowed the scope of the 2017 conference resolution to members charged, rather than merely implicated in criminal acts, targeting Magashule for one. But the ANC is making a political choice on how to implement the rule as part of a process that goes beyond just Magashule according to Legal Analyst Lawson Naidoo. Lawson Naidoo: The question that arises, if he does believe that it's unconstitutional, why has he left it until now to challenge that rule when it was adopted such a long time ago, and that will speak to the issue of urgency,. And the court may well say, this is a self created urgency and dismiss his application on the basis of urgency. VO: Magashule's argument goes further, in that his application appealing the suspension was dismissed by the NEC. Carl Niehaus: The consequences for him, if that process unfolds in the way it has unfolded for President Zuma is a destruction of his political career, and then at the end, a judge comes and say, No, you're not guilty, as happened with Bongani Bongo. Lawson Naidoo: The very nature of this stepaside resolution and process is designed as a precautionary measure and in any event, the principle of innocence until proven guilty, is a matter that pertains in criminal litigation, not in civil litigation, which this constitutes. So Mr. Magashule will surely be guaranteed the right to a fair trial. The only thing that the ANC needs to establish here is that he has been charged, therefore the step-aside rule kicks in. VO: Magashule has been a top scorer in the ANC, rising to the "all powerful position" of Secretary General, and determined to retain that power to the bitter end, he is challenging Ramaphosa head on. Sandile Swana: So Ace says, I suspended Cyril, because I was satisfied that he has done wrong. That is what he says in his court papers. He must be satisfied as the Secretary General. Carl: That situation where there are bank accounts of the CR 17 campaign, that are closed, does not become a critical issue for the majority of the National Executive Committee of the ANC to address and that indicates to us there is not even handedness, certain people are being targeted. Link: Cyril Ramaphosa - enormous wealth, links to big capital. That's his weakness, his detractors say. Ah, but not so fast. The vocal champions of the so called radical economic transformation faction are themselves often accused of corruption. So who has broken the offside rule? Carl Niehaus: If there are allegations of stealing, let action be taken, but don't equate radical economic transformation with stealing. Radical economic transformation is the official economic policy programme of the ANC. Bongani Bingwa: But many of its champions within the ANC are the same people who are accused of enabling state capture, for example, to thrive for so long. Carl Niehaus: Why are those people being accused? Because there’s selective targeting of them, while others who are not promoting radical economic transformation are left off the hook. VO: President Ramaphosa has been pursuing reform in state law enforcement agencies, empowering them to tackle corruption. Magashule contends that the main goal is to root him out and clear the way for a Ramaphosa triumph in the 2022 ANC elections. POINT 30 IN MAGASHULE’S AFFIDAVIT Sandile Swana: But a lot of the success that has been achieved in Cyril getting the majority has been by recruiting the very members of Ace's faction. They know that all the benefits are now with Cyril. VO: The RET faction is characterised by former President Jacob Zuma. At the resumption of his trial on corruption charges related to the Arms Deal, his disciples within the ANC, including Magashule, made a show of force,( … sound ups on Ace.. Ace chant…) and the fans rallied behind them. (crowd shots etc.. Vox: I support the SG because he’s our general secretary elected in the conference until we are told that he is guilty by doing 1-2-3,then we will decide otherwise then. VO: The Zuma trial is proving to be a convenient platform for the RET faction to galvanise their supporters. Political analyst, Professor Susan Booysen, maintains that radical economic transformation in their hands lacks credibility. Susan Booysen: I've just seen too many years where they have been doing virtually nothing. Bongani Bingwa: The RET faction says it's not for lack of trying. Zuma tried his best, he tried infrastructure development, he tried free education. All of those now are being rolled back. Susan Booysen: I believe certainly infrastructure development were, had as much attention in Mbeki's days as well. It was not a zuma invention. It was a grand exit point of Zuma to bring in, fee free education at a time and in a way when he needed, really needed something to build his legacy Link: Ace Magashule's suspension was the yellow card, but he's carried on the attack. It's the ultimate game of brinkmanship. So will he be shown the red card? Sandile Swana: Politically it's tricky, because you must look at the tactics of Cyril Ramaphosa, because he's the one who fired Malema, so he is unlikely to repeat that mistake.So I think that they will want to cut the wings of Ace and make him a very tame entity inside the ANC. Carl: The Secretary General will not be out of the game. This is not a football game. This is a liberation movement with a membership, and ultimately, it is not some referee with a set of cards in his upper pocket who will determine the future, but the members of the African National Congress. Bongani Bingwa:. If it were to go Ace Magashule's way, that would be a headache for the party. Lawson Naidoo: It would set a precedent, then the ANC would be effectively back to square one in how they're going to deal with corrupt elements within their membership. Battle for the ANC Roundup Susan Booysen: All indications are that the Magashule team hasn't got what it takes to clinch those goals. I think Ramaphosa's people believe they're lining up because they've had territorial advantage for much of the game. And it is really not a pretty sight to see these two [unclear] teams play,and there is going to be a winner at this stage. It looks like the Ramaphosa people.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The ANC is going into extra time in the contest between President Cyril Ramaphosa and Secretary General Ace Magashule. Both have ordered the suspension of the other, a tight match is poised at 1-1.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Ace has set out his game plan with his affidavit lodged at the Gauteng High Court. He is appealing his suspension, citing rule 25.70 of the ANC Constitution, which incorporates the step-aside rule, arguing that it was not implemented in accordance with ANC resolutions - and restates that constitutionally he should be regarded as innocent until proven guilty. Could this prove to be a massive own goal scored by the ANC? Even though he was ordered to stay silent, on 17th May after Former President Zuma’s appearance at the Pietermaritzburg High Court, Magashule went on the attack again - appealing to members (fans) to come en-masse, show their support, on May 26th. Covid-19 restrictions allowing, that day could show if Magashule has actually got the grassroots support, he claims to have, to back up the pressure he is putting on Ramaphosa’s leadership. On the other side, there is pressure on the ANC to show Magashule the red card. After all, he has refused to step aside and to apologise for trying to suspend President Ramaphosa.
metadata.Summary: What next? Magashule insists that there are processes that haven't been followed and that according to the NEC's resolutions he has not been treated fairly. He is going to appeal. His heart, his mind, his soul belongs to the ANC and according to him, nothing will make him leave his beloved party. He openly accused the Ramaphosa team of buying conference votes at Nasrec for Ramaphosa’s election as leader. Magashule says that there are more dominant factions in the ANC who are getting their way. He sees himself as a victim and as a target of those factions who are out to get Ramaphosa a second term. In all this subterfuge and confusion does Ace have a point? What can he do next? Are his governing days over, or can he win through in extra-time? To what lengths will he go and what can he actually do, politically and legally? Outside of the ANC arena, with regards to his court case on the Free State Asbestos charges, Magashule firmly states that he is innocent and has done nothing wrong, that he can't wait for his court case where there will be surprise witnesses. Story Treatment We will tell the story using soccer metaphors, interspersing football terms in the narrative: Goals, own goals, penalties, throw ins, tactics, extra time, injury time, halftime, fulltime whistle, red card, sent off, yellow card, fans, support of the, great save, tackle, foul etc, etc This is also a reference to how Magashule got the name ‘Ace’ – from his nickname in his old soccer playing days/ An idea for on-camera links is to have the presenter speak into a mic, pitch-side and in the stands sitting like a soccer commentator. We need to find a football field for this where we can also shoot atmospheric shots of the football pitch and goal nets.
metadata.Further information: This is a pivotal moment for the ANC, as President Ramaphosa stands victorious against his arch rival and detractor Magashule, as the ANC stand behind their leader in a show of resolution against corruption and wrong doing. But what skeletons lie in the Ramaphosa cupboard that can come back to haunt him? As the the ANC is now, who has won and who has lost - have there even been winners and losers or is it a case of gains and losses? The main gain if one looks at it that way is a relook at the existence of the ANC, the raison d'etre versus the power politics and the factionalism. Perhaps we have Ace Magashule to thank for this moment of possible clarity and a new, a real, New Dawn that could emerge from this. On face value Ramaphosa has doggedly pursued reform of law enforcement agencies like the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA), SA Revenue Service (SARS) and Asset Forfeiture Unit (AFU), to finally drive out corruption, and his competition. However, in Ramaphosa’s three years plus at the ANC’s helm, the “radical economic transformation” faction have thrived and exploited his weaknesses. These include his wealth and links to big capital, and the dirt within his cleanup faction. Over the last 27 years we have heard many allegations of corruption within the government all involving multimillion rand deals that go astray. But when we look back, how many of the people who have been implicated have paid the price or been held accountable when facing the law? They can be counted on one hand. The very essence of the corruption and collusion to ensure that those implicated remained untouched, went as far as manipulation of prosecuting authorities. Recently though there does appear to have been some headway under continued pressure on accused party members - to comply with ANC rules for the sake of solidarity in the movement – for instance, the high profile step aside by Provincial Deputy Chairperson of the ANC in KZN, Mike Mabuyakhulu,. Interviews: Carl Niehaus [ Confirmed ] Spokeperson: Umkhonto We Sizwe Military Veterans Association (MKMVA) Sandile Swana [ confirmed ] Political analyst Swana states that this could be a time of reckoning for the ANC, going back to what Mbekhi said concerning the raison d’etre of the ANC – he suggests the three day retreat that has been suggested is an opportunity for the ANC to look inwardly to politically and morally reformulate the ANC’s core purpose and root out the indemic and systemic corruption – or it might just be used as a platform to cement the divided factions. Susan Booysen [ confirmed ] Political analyst Lawson Naidoo [ confirmed ] Legal analyst or Benedict Phiri Legal analyst Will breakdown the veracity of Magashule’s Affidafit and court application for his appeal – some legal analysts believe he has strong grounds for appeal and that the ANC may have blundered. The ANC are not willing to speak on camera at present but have put out a media response (which we have) that they will oppose Magashule’s application
